text:
zoe: Bringing camera gear for the conference demo. Anyone have tips for flying with DSLR + lenses? worried about checked-bag risk.

marc: Carry-on everything if you can. TSA bins are annoying but I'd rather gate-check a cheap bag than risk a lens in the hold.

anita: Put lens caps and a small silica packet in each pouch. Also label gear with your name + phone.

carlos: If your carry-on is heavy, ask the gate agent to gate-check the hard case instead of dropping it in the cargo hold. Sometimes they hang onto it.

zoe: Does anyone use a Pelican-style hard case as carry-on? size/weight concerns?

marc: I do. Mine fits overhead on most narrowbodies but can be tight on regional jets. Pack a light jacket inside the case to shore up gaps.

anita: Also scan serial numbers and email them to yourself + the travel alias. Makes insurance claims easier.

travel-insurance-bot: Reminder: for company reimbursement, declare expensive equipment in the pre-trip form and attach photos of serials. Accidental damage while traveling may be covered by travel insurance if declared.

zoe: Any tricks for passing through security quickly? I hate the whole separate-laptop thing with 3 lenses.

carlos: Use a laptop bag with a quick-access compartment. Put lenses in a padded organizer that slides out so you can pull the whole organizer instead of unloading everything.

anita: Also try TSA PreCheck if you travel a lot; you can keep electronics in the bag and skip the shoe dance.

marc: Last tip: bring zip-locks for small screws and caps, and a microfiber cloth for quick lens cleaning.

zoe: Thanks all. Filing serials now and will mark the pre-trip form. Less nervous about the flight. :camera:
